title: Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) Program — Overview and definition
t: Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) Program — Overview and definition
description: Converts CAD models into machining strategies, operations, and verified G-code.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Converts CAD models into machining strategies, operations, and verified G-code. A CAM program defines stock, fixtures, tools, and operations (facing, pocketing, profiling, drilling, 3+2 and 5-axis), computes feeds and speeds, and post-processes to machine-specific G-code. Real implementations include FreeCAD Path, Fusion manufacturing, and Mastercam. It simulates material removal, detects collisions and gouges, and verifies code before it reaches the machine.
capabilities: 2.5-axis to 5-axis milling, turning, and mill-turn strategies
Feed/speed calculation from tool and material databases
Stock simulation with gouge and collision detection
Machine-specific post-processors producing G-code
Setup sheets and tool lists for the operator

Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (2.5-axis to 5-axis milling, turning, and mill-turn strategies). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: 2.5-axis to 5-axis milling, turning, and mill-turn strategies and Feed/speed calculation from tool and material databases.
